siremroke: an administrative title; an important dignity connected with the central administration
ḫrpḫne: 'governor' of a locality according to Griffith; 'mayor' according to Török
pke: noun in divine benediction formulas; it must carry a positive or laudatory value; in the amuletic oracular decrees it seems linked to a kind of blessing, in parallel with wte 'life (?)'
qor-o: predicated form of qore: 'it is the ruler', from *qore-lo ([kʷur-lu] > [kʷur-ru]) after assimilation and haplography
nse doke: ns(e) 'sacrifice' followed by the positive adjective doke (good, favourable, abundant, etc.): the offering wished for the deceased in benediction formula E (14 occurrences)
mte: (1) noun: "child"; (2) title: "page (?)"; (3) adjective: "small", "young", "the younger" in personal names
teter: a priestly title linked with the cults of Amun, Amanap, Mash, Mut and Ḫsḫseli
qorene: frequent title; probably derived from qore 'king' with the nominal suffix -ne
qorise: genitive of qore 'king' ('of the king'), produced by progressive assimilation of the article: qore + -li + -se = [kʷurliṣ] > [kʷurriṣ] or [kʷuriṣ]; a title in REM 0137
smlo (1): a title (?); probably s-mlo, from s 'man' + mlo 'good', here with a more specific social sense
ssimete: a priestly office, or at least one attached to the service of a temple
snte: a high-ranking priestly title, notably of the high priests of Amanap at Karanog
tewiseti: a loan from Demotic t(3)-wšt.t 'adoration', 'praise' (Greek τὸ προσκύνημα)
dik: 'over the whole distance'; X-k(e) : dik : Y-yte 'from X all the way to Y'
ḫrpḫe: denoting authority; 'to order, to command' (the sense generally proposed since Priese 1971)
slẖs: a priestly title of the clergy of Amanap; an intermediate office
soni: a priestly title associated with the cults of Amun, Amanap and Mash
trtekese: a priestly title of the 3rd century AD, the only known office linked with the cult of Apedemak, held by members of the royal family
stmdese: title of an important official of the viceroy's office
ẖe (1): a verb of benediction formula A; 'to drink' seems the preferable sense
beltore: the phrase bele beltore must denote a valuable object; a funerary gift according to Millet
ḫbḫne: title of an official attached to the royal house
ttne: a frequent title of an official attached to the royal household
beloloke: an important priestly title, associated with the cult of Amanap
tqi: a priestly title linked with the cults of Amanap and Mash
qoleb: plural demonstrative corresponding to singular qo or qoli (pronoun qo followed by the plural determiner -leb); 'these'
mdese: a relation between a royal and a god, probably 'direct descendant'
ḫlbine: a title dependent on the viceroy (pesetolise)
